correctness.rationale: For \(A=[[\alpha,\beta],[\gamma,\delta]]\), every nilpotent \(N=[[a,b],[c,-a]]\) satisfies \(a^2+bc=0\), and \(\det(A-N)=\det A+(\alpha-\delta)a+\gamma b+\beta c\). Projectivizing the nilpotent cone gives \(q+1\) rays parametrized by \([u:v]\mapsto[-uv:u^2:-v^2]\). The linear functional vanishes on such a ray exactly when \([u:v]\) is an eigenline of \(A\). If \(\det A\ne0\), each nonzero-functional ray contributes exactly one bad scalar multiple; if \(\det A=0\), each zero-functional ray contributes all \(q-1\) nonzero multiples plus the origin. This yields the two formulas. Exhaustive checks for \(q=2,3,5,7\) agree exactly.

value.rationale: The count is a natural quantitative refinement of the current t-fine existence property. It completely classifies representation multiplicity in the smallest nontrivial full matrix algebra by the intrinsic eigenline statistic, produces the sharp universal lower bound \((q-1)^2\), and identifies all extremal similarity types. This provides structural information that existence alone does not supply.
